content.summary: Guideline text addresses dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for acute coronary syndromes (ACS), recommending aspirin plus a potent P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor) as the default DAPT strategy. Clopidogrel is noted as less effective and reserved for contraindications, lack of availability, or some high-bleeding-risk/older patients. Prasugrel is preferred over ticagrelor in ACS patients proceeding to PCI based on head-to-head trial data. The section 6.1.2 discusses timing of loading dose of oral antiplatelet therapy, noting that both aspirin and oral P2Y12 inhibitors achieve more rapid platelet inhibition after an oral loading dose and reviews evidence (including ATLANTIC) regarding pre-treatment vs in-lab loading strategies for suspected STEMI/PPCI.
recommendations: Default DAPT for ACS: aspirin + potent P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor).
Use clopidogrel only if prasugrel/ticagrelor contraindicated/unavailable or in selected high-bleeding-risk or older patients.
Prefer prasugrel to ticagrelor for ACS patients who proceed to PCI (based on ISAR-REACT 5 RCT data).

Caution with routine pre-treatment with P2Y12 inhibitors when coronary anatomy is unknown; large-scale randomized evidence is lacking and pre-treatment may be particularly relevant in patients at high bleeding risk or on oral anticoagulants.
sections_present: 6.1.2 Timing of loading dose of oral antiplatelet therapy
6.1.2.1 Pre-treatment in patients with suspected ST-elevation myocardial infarction
clinical_points: DAPT includes aspirin + P2Y12 receptor inhibitor; prasugrel/ticagrelor preferred over clopidogrel due to greater and more consistent platelet inhibition.
ISAR-REACT 5 showed lower composite endpoint (death, MI, stroke) with prasugrel vs ticagrelor when used as the DAPT P2Y12 agent in ACS patients planned for invasive evaluation.

Pre-treatment (administration of P2Y12 inhibitor before angiography) has hypothesized benefit but lacks robust large-scale trial support; ATLANTIC evaluated timing in STEMI/PPCI and did not meet its primary endpoint for the pre-treatment strategy.
content.notes: Text emphasizes timing of loading doses and the balance between ischemic benefit and bleeding risk; highlights populations where clopidogrel may still be considered (e.g., older patients, high bleeding risk).

Associated Conditions: Patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) / primary PCI (PPCI)
genes.context: Referred to throughout as the P2Y12 receptor targeted by oral antiplatelet drugs (prasugrel, ticagrelor, clopidogrel); discussion centers on use and timing of P2Y12 receptor inhibitor loading in ACS/STEMI and PCI settings.
